claims.claim: The 2006 Amazon Soy Moratorium prevented roughly 18,000 square kilometers of deforestation over its first decade (2006-2016).
claims.episode_span: A 2020 Nature Food paper ... estimated that the moratorium reduced annual deforestation rates in soy-suitable Amazon locations by 0.66 percentage points, sparing roughly 18,000 square kilometers between 2006 and 2016.
claims.source_title: Brazil’s Amazon Soy Moratorium reduced deforestation
claims.supporting_quote: We show that the ASM reduced deforestation in soy-suitable locations in the Amazon by 0.66 ± 0.32 percentage points relative to a counterfactual control, preventing 18,000 ± 9,000 km 2 of deforestation over its first decade (2006–2016).

claims.claim: Before the moratorium roughly 30 percent of Amazon soy expansion occurred on directly deforested land; after the agreement the share fell to about 1 percent.
claims.episode_span: Early compliance data showed the share of soy expansion occurring on newly deforested Amazon land fell from about 30 percent in 2001–2006 to roughly 1 percent by 2014.
claims.supporting_quote: before the 2006 moratorium, ~30% of Amazon soy expansion occurred via direct deforestation (2001–2006: 1 Mha expansion), falling to ~1% after (by 2014, additional 1.3 Mha expansion with almost no new forest clearing)
